facts.fact: 英式圣诞晚餐必要环节：拉彩包、戴易破纸皇冠、念让人失望的笑话；其他菜可省，彩包笑话不能省
facts.anchor: An important part of any British Christmas dinner is pulling crackers, donning easily torn paper crowns and reading out underwhelming jokes.

facts.fact: 小爆炸加老套笑话给晚餐加入“表演”成分，让每个人短暂当主角；举例如 “Elf and safety”
facts.anchor: Tiny explosions followed by cheesy gags adds the ingredient of performance to Christmas dinner, briefly making everyone a star.

facts.fact: 早期彩包里装的是浪漫诗歌而非笑话：夸张华丽的维多利亚诗，由被压榨的打油诗写手批量生产
facts.anchor: In the early days of Christmas crackers, they contained romantic poetry rather than jokes.

facts.fact: 笑话直到一战之后才出现，部分原因是娱乐选择变多（有了留声机就没人听一桌人念烂诗）
facts.anchor: It was only in the years following the First World War that jokes began showing up.

facts.fact: 百年前彩包里最早的笑话今天仍勉强可用，例：What do solicitors wear to work? / Lawsuits!
facts.anchor: some of the earliest ones found in century-old crackers would just about work today

facts.fact: 圣诞是家庭场合，好彩包笑话须几代人都懂：语言简单、文字游戏基础、不要太智性或冷僻；反例 “You are having an ex’s tinsel crisis”
facts.anchor: Christmas is a family occasion, so a good cracker joke needs to be understood by multiple generations of people.

facts.fact: 过去在派对上“来一段”很流行，直到 1960 年代娱乐还很糟；那是 social awkwardness 与 cringe 概念之前
facts.anchor: The idea of ‘doing a turn’ at a party used to be a lot more popular

facts.fact: 如今标准高、到处是镜头、对演砸容忍度低，表演变得令人畏惧；作者认为可惜，并给出脱身条款（the second-best festive Claus）
facts.anchor: This has made performing a lot more intimidating as a prospect for a lot of people

facts.fact: 结尾包袱：为什么圣诞让人自我感觉良好？To boost their elf-esteem（self-esteem 换成 elf）
